quests.question: Not until the results were published _____ the scale of the problem become clear.
quests.explanation: With "not until" at the start of a sentence, the main clause is inverted, so the auxiliary "did" comes before the subject. The main verb "become" returns to the base form.

quests.question: If the government _____ to raise taxes further, many small firms could close.
quests.explanation: "If + were to" talks about an unlikely or hypothetical future event. The structure is formal and often used in discussions of possible policy changes.

quests.question: _____ for the train, I ran into an old classmate.
quests.explanation: After "while", a participle clause can replace a full clause when the subject is the same. The -ing form shows that the action was in progress.

quests.question: The reason _____ I called is to confirm your booking.
quests.explanation: After the noun "reason", the relative word is "why". "Because" would repeat the idea of cause and cannot introduce this clause.

quests.question: The agency _____ I booked the tour has closed down.
quests.explanation: In formal English, the preposition can come before the relative pronoun "which" when the noun is a thing. "That" and "whom" cannot follow a preposition in this way.

quests.question: I'm writing to enquire _____ the availability of rooms in July.
quests.explanation: "Enquire about" means to ask for information on a topic. "Enquire after" is used for asking about someone's health.

quests.question: Please switch off all devices _____ to take-off.
quests.explanation: "Prior to" is a formal way of saying "before", and it needs the word "to" after it. "Previous" is an adjective and does not combine with "to" like this.

quests.question: All staff must act _____ the company's safety regulations.
quests.explanation: "In accordance with" means following a rule or law. The phrase has a fixed form, and "according to" would refer to a source of information instead.

quests.question: We apologise for any _____ this may have caused.
quests.explanation: After "any" we need a noun, and "inconvenience" is the noun that names the problem caused. The adjective form describes a thing but cannot follow "any".

quests.question: Could you explain that _____? I didn't quite follow.
quests.explanation: "Further" means more or in greater detail, and it is used for abstract ideas. "Farther" is for physical distance.

quests.question: I overslept and _____ the first train, so I arrived late.
quests.explanation: We "miss" a train, bus or flight when we are too late to catch it. "Lose" is used for things that we can no longer find or keep.

quests.question: Thieves _____ jewellery worth thousands of pounds from the shop.
quests.explanation: We steal things but rob people or places, so the object "jewellery" requires "stole". "Burgle" refers to breaking into a building.

quests.question: Over two hundred volunteers took _____ in the clean-up.
quests.explanation: "Take part in" means to participate in an activity. "Take place" means to happen, and it has no object after "in".

quests.question: The strike caused _____ disruption to commuters.
quests.explanation: "Disruption" is uncountable here, so we need a quantifier for uncountable nouns. "A great many", "many" and "a number of" belong with plural countable nouns.

quests.question: She is _____ the most experienced person on the team.
quests.explanation: "Easily" is used as an adverb before a superlative to say that something is clearly the best. It strengthens the comparison.

quests.question: The twins look so _____ that even their teachers confuse them.
quests.explanation: "Alike" is an adjective used after a verb to say that two things are very similar. "Like" would need a noun or pronoun after it.

quests.question: He _____ have taken the keys; he was out of town all week.
quests.explanation: "Can't have" + past participle expresses a strong belief that something was impossible. The evidence, that he was away, supports this conclusion.

quests.question: The invoice _____ sent last week, but it never arrived.
quests.explanation: "Should have been" + past participle is a passive modal that talks about something that was expected but did not happen. The invoice is the thing that receives the action.

quests.question: We can't risk _____ the client by delivering late again.
quests.explanation: The verb "risk" is followed by an -ing form. The same pattern appears with avoid, consider and admit.

quests.question: A _____ of the staff voted against the plan, so it did not pass.
quests.explanation: "A majority of" is a noun phrase meaning more than half. "Most" cannot be used after the article "a".

quests.question: Almost nobody believed in the plan, and _____ people were willing to invest.
quests.explanation: "Few" has a negative sense of not enough and fits "almost nobody". "A few" would suggest a positive number, and "little" is for uncountable nouns.

quests.question: Some employees prefer working from home; _____ prefer the office.
quests.explanation: "Others" is a pronoun that refers to some more of the same group without naming them. "Other" is an adjective and needs a noun after it.

quests.question: The meeting has been brought _____ to Tuesday because of the holiday.
quests.explanation: "Bring forward" means to move an event to an earlier time. It is the opposite of "put back" and is often confused with "push back".

quests.question: Once the system _____ updated, you will need to log in again.
quests.explanation: After "once", we use a present tense to talk about the future, so the present perfect passive fits the completed update. "Will" is not used in a time clause.

quests.question: Much as I admire her work, I _____ agree with her conclusions.
quests.explanation: "Much as" introduces a concession, like "although", and the main clause expresses disagreement. "Can't agree" is the standard way to say it.

quests.question: Nobody called while I was out, _____?
quests.explanation: "Nobody" is already negative, so the tag must be positive. We use "they" to refer to "nobody" in a tag question.

quests.question: The elderly _____ often at greater risk during heatwaves.
quests.explanation: "The elderly" refers to a group of people, so it is plural and takes "are". Other examples include "the young" and "the poor".

quests.question: The hotel was spotless and the staff were friendly; _____, the location was ideal.
quests.explanation: "In addition" adds a further positive point to the list. The other linkers show contrast, replacement or a condition.

quests.question: _____ how busy you are, please make time to read this.
quests.explanation: "No matter how" means "it doesn't matter to what extent". "Whatever" cannot be followed directly by "how".

quests.question: I couldn't help _____ when he fell into the pond.
quests.explanation: "Can't help" is followed by an -ing form and means that you cannot stop yourself from doing something. It is a fixed pattern.
